correctness.rationale: For n≥4, symmetric 2n normals at latitudes ±1/√3 are exactly spherical 3-designs (all monomials through degree 3 by Fourier cancellation and odd-z symmetry). The equatorial regular n-gon with radius a_n and two poles ±b_n, where a_n²=4π/(√3 n sin(2π/n)) and b_n=√2a_n cos(π/n), has 2n triangular facets of area 2π/n with precisely those outward unit normals. Surface-area uniqueness and symmetry fix the centered Minkowski polytope. All facet offsets are b_n/√3 and the pole circumradius is b_n for n≥4. Therefore d_H(P_n,B_3)=max(b_n−1,1−b_n/√3)=b_n−1, with b_n²=(4/√3)(π/n cot(π/n)), strictly increasing since x cot x decreases; volume 4πb_n/(3√3) grows. The limit is 2/3^(1/4)−1. Rebuilt convex hulls n=4..80: 2n triangular facets; largest unit-normal error <3.1e−15, offset discrepancy <4.5e−16, surface discrepancy <2.7e−14. Infinite strict monotonicity derives from calculus, not the finite hull sweep.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks do not establish the universal theorem without the analytical/chain argument given; code proof obligations were reconstructed separately.
